## RULING 261 — what is sold, to whom, and the four constraints that carry neutrality

*`R-0261` · AMENDED · author_explicit · 2026-09-03 · also cited as `RULING 261`, `R261`, `R-261`*

- **supersedes_full** → `R-0120`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0160`
- **related_to** → `R-0126`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0142`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-C-reaction-capture-moderation-runs-before-any-export`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-C-signal-integrity-every-export-reports-its-confidence-mix`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0019`
- **sets** `business.sales_window` = `in-cycle-allowed-four-constraints`
- **sets** `business.exclusivity` = `never-exclusive`
- **sets** `business.buyer_composition` = `not-an-obligation`

**The product licenses anonymous reader-attention signal — aggregate reactions and query interest — and nothing else. Campaign-finance data never enters an export, an aggregate or anything sold, from any source. Nothing collected before the line in the sand is ever sold.**

Sean's words, which are the ruling: *"We will never sell exclusively. I will solicit equally. Whether they buy is up to them — if 65% of buyers end up on one side, that is not something I can control so long as the solicitation was equal."*

**Neutrality is carried by four constraints, and they are the whole of it:**
1. **Equal solicitation.** The offer goes out equally, by contest, and the solicitation ledger (`lib/business/solicitation-ledger.ts`) records to whom, when, at what published rate, and which contest — reconciled per contest so anyone can see at a glance that both sides were approached. The ledger shares no joinable column with reader data.
2. **Published uniform rates.** Uniform within buyer category, published, non-negotiable; every rate is a catalog entry, never a number typed on an offer.
3. **Never exclusive.** Not to a campaign, party, committee or vendor, and not for a window of time. There is no price at which exclusivity is available.
4. **No off-catalog bespoke cuts for any single buyer.**

Three constraints are artifacts and verify themselves; equal solicitation is a behaviour, and the ledger is its proof. **Buyer composition is not an obligation** — a skewed customer list is a fact about the market, and the only ways to "fix" it are to screen customers by politics or to claim a control nobody has.

**Every export reports its confidence mix** — counts by verification tier (device-attested, SMS-verified, address-validated, unverified), engagement-weighted and raw — never a single blended number. **Moderation runs before any export.** Ripcorded data never enters a sold aggregate until the question closes.

**Sales are open to any buyer at the published uniform rate, in cycle.** RULING 160 (2026-08-25), carried whole into this ruling, allowed in-cycle sales as standing policy; the author confirmed on 2026-09-03 that he does not screen buyers — anyone who wants the aggregate signal buys it at the catalog rate. The pilot-scoped "nothing until after November 3" posture is superseded and re-imported nowhere. Neutrality is not carried by choosing customers; it is carried by the four constraints above. This governs the aggregate reaction and interest signal only — campaign-finance data is still walled out of everything sold, and no exclusive or bespoke deal exists at any price.

Activation Level 5 (agents executing records requests and external communications) is removed from the architecture. Level 4 automatic publishing, deferred past 2026-11-03 by RULING 215, is now authorized (RULING 292, decision): information passing our existing verification and publication requirements auto-publishes through the production data plane, genuine official .gov sources qualify once their data passes the required checks, and Level 5 stays removed. <!-- expected-future: 2026-11-03 general election day; verified against lib/ballot/election-dates.ts. -->
